Subject: Post-demo: Reliability & SLO follow-up / next tests

Thanks for taking the demo earlier — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the reliability tests you asked about (uptime, rate limits, error budgets, and failover behavior):

Summary from the demo:
- Redwood provides a hosted inference API plus Dedicated pools; we showed a canonical routing setup that falls back to smaller model variants to maintain availability under load.
- Current hosted SLOs: 99.95% monthly uptime for the hosted API, with enterprise SLAs available for Dedicated.
- Built-in protections: adaptive rate limiting, automatic prefix/KV caching, and model-variant fallback for graceful degradation.

Competitive points you asked us to highlight vs hyperscalers/other inference APIs:
- Deterministic serving runtime tuned for inference (continuous batching, kernel selection) vs general-purpose endpoints.
- Predictable reserved throughput (Dedicated) vs noisy multi-tenant endpoints on hyperscalers.
- Transparent error budgets and per-route metrics surfaced in Console; you get token-level cost/latency breakdowns for root-cause analysis.

Proposed technical tests (we suggest running these in order):
1) Throughput stability: sustained QPS for 30m at your expected peak with a 10% headroom burst. Acceptance: P95 latency < 800ms and error rate < 0.1%.
2) Spike/burst behavior: sudden 5x traffic spike for 5m to validate rate limiting / graceful degrade.
3) Failover test: simulate primary-region outage and validate cross-region failover & model-variant fallback. Measure time-to-recover and cold-start penalty on KV cache.
4) Error-budget burn: induce transient errors and confirm alerting and automatic fallbacks behave as expected.

Attachments: I attached the SLO comparison sheet and a short test plan (stubs attached below).

Ask: Please confirm the right technical contact for running the tests (IP whitelists and dataset access), and whether you want us to run the tests from a Hosted trial account or spin up a Dedicated trial for this work.

Next steps:
- If you want Dedicated testing, we can provision reserved capacity for a 2-week trial starting as early as Mon 02/23.
- If hosted is fine, we can hand over test credentials by Monday and schedule the throughput test for Wed 02/25.

Thanks — looping in Rishi for technical details below.

--

Jumping in with technical answers — high-level bullets, happy to expand in a quick call: 

SLA / SLO:
- Hosted: published SLO = 99.95% monthly uptime for production endpoints; SLA credits available for paid tiers (details in the spreadsheet).
- Dedicated: we offer contractual SLAs (99.99%) depending on reserved capacity commitments — we can scope this in the contract.

Rate limits / throughput:
- Hosted defaults: 500 RPS per API key with short-term burst capacity to ~2k RPS subject to global capacity and fair-use. Token-rate limits vary by model; see the sheet for per-model guidance.
- Dedicated: capacity is reserved; we can guarantee sustained throughput (example: 10k tokens/s) and raise rate limits per agreement.

Error budgets and tooling:
- Error budget computed monthly as (1 - SLO) * total window; Console surfaces per-route error budget burn, and we expose webhook/PagerDuty integrations for alerts.

Failover and stateful behavior:
- Cross-region failover is automatic for stateless requests; for stateful sessions (KV cache) we recommend our multi-region replication option. Without replication, failover time depends on cache warm-up — expect 30–90s cutover plus cold-start latencies.
- To minimize cold starts, we support model-variant fallback (lighter quantized variants) which reduces tail latency during failover.

Suggested acceptance criteria for your tests (draft):
- Throughput stability: P95 latency < 800ms, error rate < 0.1% over 30m sustained load.
- Failover: system continues accepting requests; measured recovery time < 120s for end-to-end (including client retry/backoff).

If you confirm Dedicated trial, we'll provision a reserved pool, pre-warm models, and provide ssh/IP whitelist and test keys. Also attaching a short test-run checklist to the Drive link Marissa included.

Happy to run a 30-minute runbook review with your infra team before the test.
